9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (`**`).
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking
14: /// operator can be removed, making the code more readable.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
19: /// bar = {**foo, **{"C": 3}}
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
25: /// bar = {**foo, "C": 3}
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## References
29: /// - [Python documentation: Dictionary displays](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#dictionary-displays)
30: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
31: pub(crate) struct UnnecessarySpread;
32: 
33: impl Violation for UnnecessarySpread {
34:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::Sometimes;
35: 
36:     #[derive_message_formats]
37:     fn message(&self) -> String {
38:         "Unnecessary spread `**`".to_string()
39:     }
40: 
41:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
42:         Some("Remove unnecessary dict".to_string())
43:     }
44: }

46: /// PIE800
47: pub(crate) fn unnecessary_spread(checker: &mut Checker, dict: &ast::ExprDict) {
48:     // The first "end" is the start of the dictionary, immediately following the open bracket.
49:     let mut prev_end = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
50:     for ast::DictItem { key, value } in dict {
51:         if key.is_none() {
52:             // We only care about when the key is None which indicates a spread `**`
53:             // inside a dict.
54:             if let Expr::Dict(inner) = value {
55:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(UnnecessarySpread, value.range());
56:                 if let Some(fix) = checker.unnecessary_spread_fix(inner, prev_end) {
57:                     diagnostic.set_fix(fix);
58:                 }
59:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
60:             }
61:         }
62:         prev_end = value.end();
63:     }
64: }

66: impl Checker<'_> {
67:     /// Generate a [`Fix`] to remove an unnecessary dictionary spread.
68:     fn unnecessary_spread_fix(&self, dict: &ast::ExprDict, prev_end: TextSize) -> Option<Fix> {
69:         let locator = self.locator();
70:         let contents = locator.contents();
71:         let index = locator.to_index();
72: 
73:         if usize::from(dict.range.end()) > contents.len() {
74:             return None;
75:         }

89:                 if key.start() > last_item.value.start() {
90:                     return None;
91:                 }
92:             }

94:             let mut edits = vec![];
95:             for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(last_end, contents).skip_trivia() {
96:                 match tok.kind() {
97:                     SimpleTokenKind::Comma => {
98:                         edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));
99:                     }

101:                         edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));

106:             }

108:                 // Delete the first `**{`
109:                 Edit::deletion(doublestar.start(), dict.range.start() + TextSize::from(1)),

114:             // Ex) `**{}`
115:             Some(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::deletion(
116:                 doublestar.start(),
117:                 dict.range.end(),
118:             )))
119:         }
120:     }
